newsitem.title: UK: European veg oils close lower on weak demand.
newsitem.headline: European veg oils close lower on weak demand.

text.p: Weak demand pushed all sectors of the European vegetable oil market lower on Friday with many players sidelined ahead of the weekend.
"Palm oil is down owing to lack of export business in Malaysia and soft oils are subdued mainly due to the weather market still running in Chicago," said a trader.

Data issued by Malaysian cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) which showed an increase in local exports during the first 20 days of September over the same period in August failed to stimulate the palm oil market.
SGS estimated Malaysia's palm oil exports for September 1-20 at 413,743 tonnes compared with 398,288 tonnes in Aug 1-20.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed with sellers unchanged to $5 down with no further business reported during the afternoon.
In the refined palm oil sector RBD oil closed $7.50 lower and olein $12.50 to $7.50 down.
Coconut oil failed to trade and at the close traders would only quote prices as there were no firm sellers. Based on the quoted prices sellers would be around $2.50 to $5 up on the day.
Palmkernel oil was $5 down to unchanged.
In soft oils soy oil was 1.50 to one guilders lower in a tradeless market while rape oil was unchanged to 0.25 guilders down.
In light trading Feb/Apr rape oil fetched 101.75 and May/Jul 103 guilders a 100 kilos fop ex-mill.

Although no outright business was reported in soy oil traders said Nov/Jan traded at 95 guilders in a switch with Nov/Jan rape oil at 99.75 guilders. --Jim Ballantyne, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8062
